The orthodox opinion of every religion or mage guild in Erebus holds that only rare individuals are blessed (or, in some cases, cursed) with affinity for any sort of magic. It is sacrilige to suggest that every mortal soul shares a natural gift in every precept, but this heresy happens to be true. While most men's affinities are too weak to be of much use, there are ways to awaken them. The architects of the Tower of Mastery go to great lengths to talk around this point rather than state it directly, but their ambition is let every mage match the powers of Kylorin.

[ICON_BULLET]Affinity lets a Mage cast more powerful versions of the spells within his sphere than will ever be available to those without this gift. [ICON_BULLET][ICON_BULLET]A summoner with affinity keeps the xp earned by its summons from the same sphere[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Mage Guilds only accept members who have demonstrated some affinity for at least one precept. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Nearly a quarter of mages, those the Amurites call "Petrarchs," are gifted in 2 spheres. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Decliarchs, powerful individuals gifted 3 dominions, are extremely rare. Only Kylorin, the true master of every precept, has ever shown affinity for more than 3 spheres.

This heretical offshoot of the Laeran Cord still claims to revere Oghma, but in fact they serve the angels of Ceridwen. Their Conjurers are known for causing trouble with their rituals and lack of caution.
Conjurers are like Mages that can be trained directly with no level prerequisites, but they cannot build mana nodes and are a lot more likely to miscast their spells

Gallowblight is a very deadly and contagious disease that kills most of its victims over a few horrible weeks. But those that survive are forever immune to it and are actually healthier for having gone through it.
This foul curse damns its victims to return as Undead when they die.

Elven Pox is a disease that makes the victim magically inert, keeping them from being able to use magic. It is spread by magical contact, so a mind made attempting to read the mind of a victim would contract the pox and lose the ability to use magic. This has the side effect of making the victim mostly magic immune since the pox will kill all magic that touches them.
%s1 has contracted Elven Pox from trying to use magic on %s2

[ICON_BULLET]Curse of Camulos creates an overwhelming berserker rage in the victim, often leading them into attacking others, which spread the disease. It is spread through shared pain. The rage grows as the victim causes pain. The only way to recover is to go a long period of time without causing pain or violence of any sort.

[ICON_BULLET]This disease is rarely lethal on its own, but it causes permanent rot in its victims and leaves them too weak to defend themselves. It is highly contagious, spreading through any contact with infected blood or saliva. It can quickly overtake an entire village if even one guard contracts it in combat. Certain breeds of wolves and trolls have adapted to being carriers of the disease, attacking once to infect a victims and then returning to finish off a whole settlement.

[ICON_BULLET]Cannot fall in an [LINK=SPELL_ARENA_BATTLE]Arena battle[\LINK][NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Being an Aspect of War is the highest blessing Camulos can grant, but he does not care who gets it so long as they use their power to kill. It is given at birth and cannot be revoked. All the Aspects have superhuman martial prowess, both in personal strength and in tactics. While they may not defeat whole armies on their own, in single combat are nearly invincible. Some are Good, some are Evil, and some are hostile towards both extremes, but they cannot remain neutral in any conflict for long. They are the cause of most wars, regardless of their intent. Notable Aspects of War include Arak the Erkling, Capria, Mahon the Butcher, Orthus, Magnadine, Surder, and Makhai. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Every god created seven Aspects, True Angels whose inherent affinity is exceeded only by that of the archangels or the gods themselves, and whose freedom to act in creation is not limited by The Compact. The original Aspects of War were vanquished early int he Godswar, but whenever one falls it is reincarnated as a mortal. Years can pass before an Aspect of War is reborn, but there are usually 5 to 7 active in the world at any time. The Sons of Discord try to track them individuals down and use them to cause more conflict.
[ICON_BULLET]A Spellstaff lets a unit cast twice per turn, can be broken to allow the caster to regain the ability to cast yet again
[ICON_BULLET]Allows the unit to cast High Priest Level Divine spells
[ICON_BULLET]Allows a unit with affinity to use its rank 4 spells
Divine Spells are made less effective when used by a player without the right state religion or acting in lands without the state religion

TEXT.English: The Instructors of Nantosuelta make sure that those in their charge are fully equipped for their duties, physically, mentally, and spiritually. This eliminates the costs of upgrading them.

[ICON_BULLET]The magic of Laroth binds this unit's soul to the Netherworld, so it may not be resurrected in Erebus nor return as an [LINK=UNIT_ANGEL]Angel[\LINK] or [LINK=UNIT_MANES]Demon[\LINK]. Only [LINK=SPELL_DESTROY_NETHER_BLADE]destroying[\LINK] the [LINK=EQUIPMENT_NETHER_BLADE]the Netherblade[\LINK] may break this spell.

[TAB]Among the Orcs mad men are gathering, singing songs they hope will wake sleeping Dragons. They tell tales of the Flame Lord, a great Torch Dragon whose spirit has been restless since his mistress fell and who seeks an entry into our world to regain his ancient form and take vengeance on whomever he can blame for his pain.

[TAB]Acheron the Torch Dragon has made his lair in the barbarian city of %s1. [PARAGRAPH]The rage of the Orcs has summoned him from a realm of myths beyond the ether, where Bhall imprisoned the spirit of the Flame Lord once Godswar ended, back into the physical world. [PARAGRAPH]Madmen have begun to worship this beast, and others like him whom they hope to Stir from Slumber, in place of the gods. The priests of all religions warn that this Cult of the Dragon may soon become a scourge upon our land. [PARAGRAPH]Rumor has it that Acheron rests upon a bed of unrivaled riches. Multitudes covet The Dragon's Hoard, and hundreds have lost their lives seeking it. This is all in vain. Unlike most dragon species, Torch Dragons don't collect anything. The most valuable thing found in their lairs is their unquenchable mucus, which burns for days with enough heat to consume metal, stone, and even incorporeal spirits.

Completing this ritual will cool the world, changing some of the [LINK=literal]Desert[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Plain[\LINK]s, some [LINK=literal]Plain[\LINK]s and [LINK=literal]Grassland[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Tundra[\LINK]s, some [LINK=literal]Tundra[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Snow[\LINK]s tiles, and some [LINK=literal]Raw Mana[\LINK] to [LINK=literal]Ice Mana[\LINK]. It will also spawn occasional [LINK=literal]Blizzard[\LINK]s around the map.

This ritual gives the Immortal promotion to all of the living units the caster currently owns. Try to time its creation with a time when you have a lot of units available to take advantage of the effect. The Immortal promotion only resurrects a unit once, so this doesn't grant an eternal supply of units, but it gives every unit a second chance.

Recruits 6 Hill Giants to the player's cause.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]Early explorers found it was best to avoid the massive giants that roamed the land. A bard, named Antonis of Oriel, wandered too close and was captured by a group called the Nilhorn. He offered the only gift he could for his life, he played a song. The wild giants were so entranced by his song that, when it ended, they sat unmoving and Antonis could have simply walked out of the makeshift camp they had dragged him back to. Fascinated by finding his new audience so appreciative, Antonis continued to play, and his performances became a part of the giants' nightly rituals.[PARAGRAPH:1]Antonis stayed with the Nilhorn for three years, until one of them reported seeing a Sheaim army approaching his homeland. The giants avoided any settled land and tried to convince Antonis not to return, but he left the giants and returned to defend Oriel. Although a talented musician, Antonis was an incompetent warrior and he was killed defending Oriel. When he fell, the Nilhorn came out of the forests and approached the besieged village. Both armies froze, unaccustomed to seeing giants willing to enter civilized lands. Searching the battlefield, the giants found Antonis's body, and, enraged, they set upon the Sheaim. The village defenders cheered at their new-found allies and joined in the assault.[PARAGRAPH:1]The battle was quick and the Sheaim were turned back. After it was over, the giants picked up the body of Antonis and carried it with them into the forests. The village raised a monument to their large rescuers and swore never to forget the aid they were given. The Sheaim never forgot the failed battle either, and forever avoided Oriel in their attacks.
Six allied Hill Giants will appear in the building civilization's city.

[ICON_BULLET]Make a deal with a devil, that he may come to Erebus and you may have a truce with the forces of Armageddon. (If previously defeated, they will be revived. ) Grants them [LINK=UNIT_ANAGANTIOS]their[\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_DUMANNIOS]respective[\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_RIUROS]avatars[\LINK] leading armies of their own. (Note: the loss of any leader's avatar removes that leader's traits. )[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET][LINK=UNIT_AURIC]Auric's avatar[\LINK] has affinity for whatever mana source may be present on his tile. The [LINK=BONUS_MANA_ICE]Ice mana[\LINK] from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_LETUM_FRIGUS]Letum Frigus[\LINK] will remain in New Mulyr and let him cast powerful Ice spells from within that city, but he will be less powerful if he wanders elsewhere on the map. Auric must be kept alive (or resurrected) if there is to be any hope of ascending to [LINK=UNIT_AURIC_ASCENDED]godhood[\LINK] through [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DRAW]The Draw[\LINK] and [LINK=PROJECT_ASCENSION]Ascension[\LINK] rituals.

Completing this ritual halves all your cities' populations, damages all your units and causes you to declare war on every player in the game. You will also be unable to enter diplomacy with any player you are at war with for the rest of the game. It starts [LINK=UNIT_AURIC]Auric Ulvin[\LINK] on the path to godhood that will be completed by the Ascension ritual, for which this is a prerequisite. Auric the leader gains the [LINK=TRAIT_INSANE]Insane trait[\LINK]. Auric the unit gains the [LINK=PROMOTION_IMMORTAL]Immortal[\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_CHANNELING4]Channeling IV[\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_CRAZED]Crazed[\LINK], and [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_ICE]Ice Affinity[\LINK] promotions (whereever he goes, not only when there is Ice mana on his tile). Once this ritual is complete, hostile units of [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\LINK] religion with automatically defect to Auric's side, all other players with The White Hand State religion will become his vassals, and all of his Vassals will be forced to adopt the White Hand as their state religion so long as he is alive.

There have always been men that ran toward danger. In the age of Magic, some were known as the Brotherhood of Wardens. They were a secret organization that tried to protect the citizens of Patria from cruel edicts of the Imprimator Council. They rescued elven captives from the Duchy of Dust, chattel slaves from Candlefast, and debtors from the Duchy of Glimmerhome. [PARAGRAPH]The organization started as a secular one, but the archangel Pelian the Suffering was inspired by the brave members of the brotherhood. When the rebellions began and the war started between the Empyrean, the Sanctus Inquisition and the Imprimatur Council, the Brotherhood attempted to make sure that the weak and innocent weren't destroyed in that war. [PARAGRAPH]They had middling success. Many were lost. But if they could get those they rescued back to the Duchy of Logos, they would find the tides would turn in their favor. Enemies spells were weakened, rotting wolves would lose their scent, their own endurance, and hope returned. This was the arda of Sirona and the blessing she offered for their cause. "[PARAGRAPH:2]The Brotherhood of Wardens is a cult of Sirona that teaches men that they must do whatever they can to protect the least among them. The orthodox Wardens were exterminated in Calabim lands, but Alexis encourages the spread of a heretical sect that believes the best way to protect the meek is to teach them to passively accept any form of oppression without every trying to fight back. [PARAGRAPH:2]Pelian disobeyed Sirona during the Godswar. Sirona commanded that compassion required the defense of creation, but Pelian refused to be violent and abandoned her army. After suffering a massive defeat Sirona lay nearly destroyed. As the army of Aeron closed in, Pelian returned and placed a sanctuary around Sirona. Pelian was attacked, but he still refused to fight. Instead he was torn and tortured for 21 days and bore the worst of Aeron's torments. His body is forever broken from this ordeal. But after 21 days Sirona was revived and came out of the sanctuary to rescue her archangel and scatter the army of Aeron. The breaking of the compassionate Pelian was an example to the gods that the compact was needed. [PARAGRAPH]Pelian lay recovering for centuries. It wasn't until the Age of Ice that he gazed again into creation, drawn by the calls of those suffering. There was little he could directly do, but he whispered to the great Eurabatres, who was sleeping nearby and awoke the dragon, calling him to aid those in need. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth he attempted to calm the heart of Basium, before he marched through into hell. Pelian warned that his hubris would lead him into serving Agares, or at least remove his blessed protection from creation. But Basium ignored him and marched through the Throne of Hell. Pelian wept for him and those doomed to be lost with him. [PARAGRAPH]During the Age of Invention, when the Matronae came for the worshipers of the old gods, Pelian's spirit was with the few remaining worshipers of Sirona and called for them to be non-violent. He called for calm as they stood before the Shrine of Sirona, as their statues were torn down, as their holy texts were burned and as each worshiper of Sirona that refused to forsake their goddess was executed. Then he gathered their souls and carried them to the Isle of Birds. [PARAGRAPH:2]State religion allows access to:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_TRISTAN]Tristan the Ring [\LINK] (world unit and summon)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_SIRONA]Wardens of the Meak [\LINK] (unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_BLINDED_BROTHER]Blinded Brothers [\LINK] ([LINK=CIVILIZATION_CALABIM]Calabim[\LINK] unique unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_SIRONA]Redeemer [\LINK] (unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_MERRY_DANCER]Merry Dancer [\LINK] (unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]Halves the production cost of: [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_BROTHERHOOD]Safehouse[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_SHRINE_OF_SIRONA]The Shrine of Sirona[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PALACE_ELOHIM]The Elohim Palace[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:2]Units of this faith are more likely to gain affinity for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SPIRIT]Spirit[\LINK] mana[PARAGRAPH:3]Priests and Angels of [LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]The Brotherhood of Wardens[\LINK] will have its arda most strengthened by the influence of the Brotherhood, but also strengthened to a lesser degree by [LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]The Unblemished[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]The Ringgivers[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]The House of Plenty[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_ETERNAL_CABAL]The Eternal Cabal[\LINK]. Its arda will be weakened by [LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]The Children of The One[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]The Matronae[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]The Anointed[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]The Grey Council[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]The Sons of Discord[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]The Stewards of Inequity[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]The Ember Legion[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]Cult of the Dragon[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Order[\LINK]. It will be strengthened in Good lands and weakened in Evil lands. When he obtained the Font of Life and rose again as the God Life, his nature was so changed that the Fellowship abandoned him and began worshiping his old archangel Cernunnos as their chief god. Sucellus himself actively intervened to create a new cult for himself, called the Unblemished. Many of its members were born through immaculate conception, or are the mothers of those so conceived, and manifest powerful affinity for Life. The Unblemished make the best healers in Erebus. They run hospitals that employ all the same treatments as the Grigori Medics while complimenting it with prayers from holy men who have been known to revive the dead by faith alone. The Stewards of Inequity are a cult to Mammon, although few of their members will ever realize this. Mammon prefers his follows believe that they serve only their own self interest. The Stewards hate any sort of honest work but will go to great lengths to amass fortunes. Most are already very wealthy and powerful men when they join this cult, although some are merely covetous and believe membership will help further their ambitions. Its ranks include many tax collectors, regulators, government lobbyists, almost every central banker, the upper management in most large companies, and even many priests high in the hierarchies of other faiths. Few Stewards rank high enough to ever learn of the existence of the cabal that convenes to decide the policies they all execute. Most are just happy to play their small part towards the lofty goal of making the rick richer and the poor poorer. The Anointed are a cult of psychopaths devoted to Aeron, the God of Body, Strength, Sadism, Lust, Rage, Hate, and especially premeditated Murder. All of its members enjoy violence, and view killing or mutilating the innocent as a most sacred act. Although Aeron is the patron of Berserkers, he prefers the more subtle arts of the most cold hearted assassins. The cult is dominated by small group of powerful warriors called The Occisors. There is not much structure in this religion, although its members are encouraged to attain elite positions in other evil organizations. Aeron is best known as the Lord of Murder. His worshipers are usually terrifyingly powerful warriors, who could easily win most fair fights but pride themselves in never fighting fair. They prefer to strike the killing blows before their targets realize they are enemies. Aeron is also known as Maiden Friend; he has a great weakness for physical beauty, which his worshipers often inherit. They are often unwilling to harm those of great beauty. [PARAGRAPH:2]State religion allows access to:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_DANAG]Danag the Faithful[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_SIR_HALEWYN]Sir Halewyn[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_LUIDAG]Luidag the Rag[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]Halves the production cost of: [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_HUNTING_LODGE]Hunting Lodges[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_GOVERNORS_MANOR]Governor's Manors[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_DUNGEON]Dungeons[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PILLAR_OF_CHAINS]The Pillar of Chains[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_SCHOOL_OF_SADISM]The School of Sadism[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PALACE_CALABIM]The Calabim Palace[\LINK][PARAGRAPH:2]Units of this faith are more likely to gain affinity for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_BODY]Body[\LINK] mana.[PARAGRAPH:3]The Candy Shop[PARAGRAPH:2]Sunlight filtered through the temple's stained-glass windows and cast images of angels and saints on the western wall. Within the temple parishioners shuffled uncomfortably in their pews as the Literal droned on with his sermon. The service was nearly over, and the children were even more restless than the adults. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat between her father and her younger brother, Artan. She was nine years old and like most of the children in the temple, was daydreaming about the many treats of the candy shop that sat in the temple's shadow. While others prayed she imagined pine nuts dipped in honey and sugar, gingerbread men and fingers sticky with pecan brittle. [PARAGRAPH]But they would only visit the candy shop if they were good during the service. It was this promise that kept the children quiet and still on Sunday mornings. It was as much a part of the children's religious experience as the Literals welcoming invocation or the brilliant arches of light that crossed the temple's dusty lofts. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung his feet beneath the pew, risking kicking either the pew in front of him or the bottom of his seat. Amelie squeezed his hand and gave him a threatening look. Around the temple many mothers gave similar looks to their children, and Amelie's was as practiced and effective as any of them. [PARAGRAPH]The sermon closed with a final adulation and the worshipers rose to make their way out of the temple. Amelie grabbed her father's hand and Artan followed quickly behind. Now allowed to talk he was full of questions, most concerning the candy shop. They had been good so yes, they would visit the shop on the way home. And they would be able to pick one, and only one, piece of candy. It was the same as every other week, but Artan and a half-dozen other children still asked their parents if they could go, and still pleaded for more than one piece, though no parent relented. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie remained quiet. She already knew her father's answers and she was trying to pick the candy she wanted from her memory of the candy shops selection. She dreamed of caramelized pears, chewy toffee, or raisins coated with sugar and cinnamon. She carefully imagined each candy as they walked down the hill from the temple to the small shop, and changed her mind at least a dozen times. This was her favorite part of the week. Her father was sober and kind and the three of them were, for a little while, a happy family. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was brightly painted with a red roof and white trim over a deep green building. The front door was white, and stood beside a large window which let those on the street glimpse shelves of glass jars filled with brightly wrapped treats. The warm shop was a welcome escape from the chill wind that threatened to bring the winter's first snowfall. [PARAGRAPH]"Remember Artan, don't touch anything. " his father warned, "Pick the piece you want and tell me, so I can ask merchant Hamish to get it for us. "[PARAGRAPH]"Yes papa. " Artan answered. [PARAGRAPH]The shop's front room smelled like gingerbread and vanilla. Other families were already picking out their treats and every child carefully considered their selection, they were stuck between the desire to try a piece of candy and the fear that if they didn't look hard enough they may overlook something new and wonderful. Amelie had a different reason to spend more time picking, she didn't want this brief time in the candy shop to end. [PARAGRAPH]Merchant Hamish wandered over to Amelie as she looked at butterscotch candies in bright wrappers. He was a small man, thin and frenetic, with a weak leg that required him to use a cane. But his boundless energy made up for his clumsy three-legged gait and he made sure everyone in the shop was taken care of. He never forgot an order, and was quick to scoop, cut or measure whatever a customer requested. He wore a red and white apron that matched the color of his shop and had a crazy shock of white hair that would look unusual on anyone else, but somehow fit the shopkeepers wide, smiling face perfectly. [PARAGRAPH]"I have some ginger bread cookies I just took out of the oven. I believe you picked one last week, and nibbled on it like a mouse as you left my shop. " Hamish said. [PARAGRAPH]"I wanted it to last longer. " Amelie explained, "What are the cookies shaped like today?"[PARAGRAPH]"There were some complaints about last week's cookies. Apparently, speaker Ides didn't appreciate having his rotund figure memorialized as a cookie. And I don't know if I can afford to keep making cookies that large. So, I switched to smaller things, like buildings in the city. There are some of the cathedral bell towers, some shaped like the temple belfry, the bridge tower, the lighthouse, and the east gate. And of course. . . " Hamish added after a pause, "maybe a few fat speaker Ides hidden in the back. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie smiled, but before she could reply another family was ready to buy and merchant Hamish was off to help them. [PARAGRAPH]Artan already had his treat, an unnaturally red candied apple. He always picked the largest treat he could find, and today was no different. He sat beside his father on a low bench in front of the window greedily devouring it. Amelie's father gave her a look that meant she had to hurry up. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie finally picked a piece of swirled vanilla and butterscotch. It was so soft she could shape it with her hands and it melted in her mouth. She made tiny bites out of the thumb sized candy as her father paid for it and they left the shop for the short walk home. [PARAGRAPH]Throughout the day Amelie continued to take tiny bites from her candy, and lied to her brother when he asked if there was any left. He finished his apple before they were out of the candy shop. By nighttime Amelie had the last bite saved in the wrapper as a treat for morning and she curled up in her blankets to sleep. [PARAGRAPH]In that grey world between sleep and wakefulness Amelie imagined a bright light in her room. She opened her eyes, but the room was dark. Her tiny bed barely fit in her room, and there was no window. The only light was from her father's room, where a lamp burned. Her door was cracked, and a sliver of pale light bled into her room from the hall. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie closed her eyes and tried to drift back to sleep. When she was again in that strange limbo before sleep the light returned. This time when she opened her eyes, the light remained. [PARAGRAPH]An angel floated above her bed. Tall and beautiful he had skin like honey and light radiated out of him as if the sun set beneath his skin. As wondrous as he appeared his face was lined with concern, and his eyes were unnaturally dark. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie pulled her blankets up above her head and curled beneath them. The angel's light shone through the thin blankets and even completely covered, Amelie could clearly see her trembling hands. But the light was mild compared to the other indications of the angel's presence. A feeling of peace and warmth radiated through the room. And though Amelie had never imagined meeting an angel before, her fear melted away. She lowered the blanket enough to see the angel's face. [PARAGRAPH]"I am truly sorry. " the angel said. His voice conveyed deep compassion and though it wasn't loud it resonated through the small house. "I tried to deliver this message to many people, but they were blind to me. "[PARAGRAPH]"Who are you?" Amelie asked. She wondered if she was dreaming, but it seemed both too real and too unlikely to be a dream. [PARAGRAPH]"I am Verchiel, herald angel of Lugus. I have come to send a message, and a warning. " the angel answered. "Your brother Artan is in great danger. He has left your house and wandered into darkness. He is already beyond my sight, and it may not be possible to save him. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat up in her bed. The sudden skip and racing of her heart convinced her that she was not asleep. "Where is he? What kind of danger?" she asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He is within the home of an Anointedor, out of the light and into the province of the god of blood. " Seeing that Amelie was confused Verchiel added, "He is in the home of an evil man. That is all I know. Lugus's influence is waning and I have very little ability to act. You may be able to save your brother, you may not, or you may die in the attempt. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie was already out of bed throwing on her shoes and coat. [PARAGRAPH]"Where is he?" Amelie asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He went to the candy shop. " Verchiel said, and for a second the angel looked afraid. Before Amelie rushed out of her room Verchiel stopped her. "I can give some small help. If you get to the temple and you hold your hand on the altar you will be safe. It is the most I can offer, though it is not much. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie rushed out of her room and into Artan's. Just as the angel said Artan was gone. His blankets were thrown aside, and his shoes and coat were missing. Amelie went back into the hall where she noticed her room was dark again, the angel was gone. But she didn't stop to consider his disappearance as she ran into her father's room. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie's father snored loudly from his bed. His lamp flickered and cast odd shadows. The room smelled like stale beer and sweat. Amelie shouted at her father, called for him, and shook him. But in his drunken delirium he did nothing but swat her away. Amelie pushed him off the bed. He crashed to the floor in a tangle of blankets, rolled over and continued snoring. Giving up, Amelie left him and headed outside onto a small landing and down the stairs to the street. [PARAGRAPH]It was an early winter night and the season's first light snowfall was settling on the city. Amelie could see her brother's tracks in the snow and she followed them along the street toward the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was only a few blocks away and it appeared as it did on all their visits. It was tidier than the surrounding buildings, and its red roof and white trim seemed at odds with the fear that clawed at Amelie as she ran. Though the front room of the shop was lost in darkness Amelie imagined that there were still rows of jars full of candy, and for a second she thought herself crazy for having rushed here in a panic. Until she noticed her brother's footprints leading up to the front porch. [PARAGRAPH]She followed them onto the porch with her heart once again racing. The roof kept the porch clear of snow, Artan's footprints ended at the porch stairs. Amelie crossed the porch, and though she had never noticed that the porch creaked in the many times she walked across it, now it seemed to cry out with each step. [PARAGRAPH]Reaching the door, she turned the knob, but it was locked. It seemed secure and untampered with. Unless someone had locked it since Artan went in, Amelie couldn't imagine how he would have gotten through. [PARAGRAPH]Walking down the porch Amelie came to the large front window. Pushing her face against the glass she looked into the room beyond. She could see the vague outlines of the room. The counter where the sales were made, the shelves covered in candy jars. What wasn't lost in darkness seemed normal. [PARAGRAPH]For the first time Amelie shivered in the cold. Though her coat was warm, she had thrown it on over her sleeping gown, which was one of her father's old shirts. It was threadbare before she got it and though it hung just past her knees, it provided little protection against the chill night air. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie walked to the end of the porch looking for anything unusual. At the very end she saw where Artan's footprints began again. He had jumped off the porch and walked around the side of the shop. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie followed the footprints around into the darkness. She had to stop and wait for her eyes to adjust, and build up her courage. There was no one on the street, but as she stood in the shop's shadow Amelie remembered that there was a guard station at the north bridge a few blocks away. If she ran there and if the guards believed her she could be back with help in fifteen, maybe twenty minutes. Deciding Artan may not be able to wait that long, she continued following the footprints around the shop. [PARAGRAPH]The back of the shop was a simple deep green wall with white trim and no doors. There was a small window set too high in the wall for Amelie to see through. But it wasn't the window or the shop that interested her, but what the tracks led to, a simple cellar door in the ground. [PARAGRAPH]The bar that usually blocked the cellar door now lay discarded beside it. Though Artan's footprints clearly led to the cellar door, there was no indication of him walking away. Amelie whispered a prayer to Lugus as she walked to the door, then hoping it was quieter than the squeaky porch, she opened it. [PARAGRAPH]Beneath the door a ladder descended into darkness. Amelie could feel warm, moist air coming out of the cellar and she was happy to see that there was a faint flickering light below. Leaning close to the opening Amelie whispered for Artan, trying to be loud enough so he would hear her, but quiet enough that someone else wouldn't. [PARAGRAPH]After waiting to see if there was any sound or response, Amelie climbed into the hole and down into the cellar. Cellars were unusual in Bourne, as the city sat between two rivers the ground was generally too wet to dig down in. Any sufficiently deep hole turned into a well. But the few she had seen had stairs leading into them, not ladders. And this ladder went down further than Amelie expected. If the candy shop had a basement, Amelie guessed that this cellar would be below it. [PARAGRAPH]The ladder ended at a hallway with a rough stone floor and slick reddish-brown walls. The ladder shaft was so small that an adult would have difficulty squeezing through, but the hallway was much larger. Looking up Amelie could see the night sky, and now that she was on the ground she could see light coming from further down the hallway. After whispering again for Artan and receiving no response she started slowly down the hallway. [PARAGRAPH]A scream echoed through the cellar so pained and shocked that Amelie nearly turned and fled back up the ladder. She couldn't imagine a person could communicate such horror in a yell, and at first thought it wasn't human. But her body went chill as she recognized the voice, it was Artan. [PARAGRAPH]Everything seemed to slow down. The smallest details leapt out at her and even though Amelie ran down the short hallway toward the screams, she felt like she was running in mud. [PARAGRAPH]The hallway continued straight with two open archways on each side. A lit lamp hung on a hook between the archways and provided the only light. Amelie only briefly glimpsed through the first two archways as she rushed by, the left contained large cages, like a kennel. Something moved in the cages, something large and covered in filth. The opposite archway was dominated by a stone table and tools and knives hung from the walls. Both rooms made Amelie more afraid. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie ran into the second room on the right, where Artan's screams were coming from. For a moment she was delighted to see that Artan stood in the middle of the room facing away from her, appearing uninjured. Amelie grabbed him and spun him around, pulling him into a hug. He jumped when she touched him and tried to push away, but as soon as he realized it was her he collapsed against her and burst into heavy, pained sobs. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't have to ask why he was crying. What was hanging on the wall stole any slight relief Amelie may have felt at the recovery of her brother. [PARAGRAPH]Once it had been a man, a massively fat man buried in rolls of flesh. But all the fat had been cut away. His chest lay open, brass eyelets had been sewn into his skin and hooks held open a bloody gaping maw that exposed the bare organs beneath. His organs were tied along his spinal column and his heart still beat from within a thin mesh of netting, his lungs expanded and shrank with each breath and the slick bloody mass of organs dumped down into coiled intestines. His lower jaw and tongue had been removed so his head was a helpless hook on the wall, and his eyes moved and watched the children with an emotion Amelie had never seen before. His arms and legs had been painfully hollowed out, leaving the bone and clinging muscle, but now only air filled the loose skin. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie opened her mouth to scream but no sound came out. [PARAGRAPH]The crack of the cellar door closing shocked Amelie into action. [PARAGRAPH]"Shut up!" she yelled at Artan, "Are you okay?" As she asked, Amelie made sure Artan stayed facing her, so he couldn't see the man hanging on the wall behind him. [PARAGRAPH]Taking deep breaths Artan coughed out his words, "I. . . want. . . to. . . go. "[PARAGRAPH]"We will be okay, calm down. I am going to take you home. " Amelie said. The man hanging on the wall continued to stare at her and Amelie wondered if he had snuck down into the cellar looking for sweets too. [PARAGRAPH]The sound of another door opening and slamming closed shocked them both. It sounded closer than the cellar door. Amelie guessed it was from whatever was straight down the hallway. She could hear someone walking toward them. It was the familiar step, step, click of the candy shop owner's cane. [PARAGRAPH]Holding Artan close Amelie dove beneath the only object in the room besides the hanging man. It was a small end table near the entrance to the room. She could hear the footsteps in the hall. She held Artan's head against her chest and tried to stay quiet. She looked at the hanging man, silently pleading with him to quit staring at where they were hiding. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp light jumped and flickered as someone lifted the lamp off its hook. Then Amelie saw Hamish's wiry legs and cane step in beside the end table. She and Artan held their breath in fear. She briefly considered rushing to Hamish for help. But nothing in the candy shop owner's demeanor seemed surprised by the man hanging on the wall, and that kept Amelie trembling and quiet beneath the end table. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish set the lamp down on top of the end table, and walked across the room to look at the hanging man. With Hamish's back to them Amelie considered running from the room. As Amelie watched, Hamish set his cane down. Then he climbed up onto the hanging man and spun around, sliding his legs down into the partially hollow legs of the hanging man and his arms into the huge bodies hollow arms. Hamish's head came just under the hanging man's upper jaw, so it appeared that Hamish was wearing the hanging man's horrified face as a cruel helmet. The hanging man only offered a muffled cry in protest, but Hamish ignored him. Instead Hamish looked delighted to be settling into the hanging man's body, wearing a living man as a thick fleshy suit. The candy maker's eyes sparkled as he ran a cord through the brass eyelets, sewing himself into the body so that only his head remained exposed. [PARAGRAPH]Too terrified to see what would happen when Hamish finished sewing himself into the body Amelie crawled out from under the end table and pulled Artan behind her. She grabbed the lamp off the end table and ran into the hallway, back toward the shaft up to the cellar door. She pushed Artan in front of her and he climbed up the ladder shaft into the darkness. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie was halfway up the ladder before she heard Hamish thundering down the hallway after them. This time there was no slow click of the cane, only thick pounding footfalls. She looked down at the pudgy flesh of the hanging man's hands and arms as Hamish grabbed the ladder and shook it. But they were almost at the top. [PARAGRAPH]Artan reached the top and tried to swing the cellar door open, but it had been barred from the outside. [PARAGRAPH]"It's locked!" Artan yelled. [PARAGRAPH] The ladder shook again as Hamish was tearing it off the wall. Both the children screamed, hoping someone outside would hear them. [PARAGRAPH]"Hold onto the sides. " Amelie yelled as the ladder threatened to collapse. [PARAGRAPH]"Come down children. " Hamish called, "You will be ripe fruit on Aeron's altar tonight. "[PARAGRAPH]At that the ladder collapsed and Amelie and Artan were left braced in the shaft. Artan slipped on the wet walls. Below them Hamish laughed in delight. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm sorry. " Artan said, and his eyes began to well up with tears. [PARAGRAPH]"Listen to me. " Amelie ordered, "Is there another door?"[PARAGRAPH]"Yes," Artan said, "straight down the hallway there are stairs leading up. But that door is barred too. "[PARAGRAPH]"I don't think so, not anymore. He couldn't have barred this door from the outside if he came down it. He had to have come through the other door. " Amelie said. She could feel herself slipping. Hamish had become quiet, but he still glared up at them with hungry, depraved eyes. [PARAGRAPH]"When I say go," Amelie said, "slide down the shaft as fast as you can and run for that door. Don't stop for anything. Just run and go to the temple, not home. In the temple put your hand on the altar and don't take it off until you are safe, he can't hurt you if you touch the altar. Do you understand?"[PARAGRAPH]Artan nodded. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie took one more look down at Hamish, then she dropped the lamp. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp smashed into the hallway floor and oil splashed out in all directions, burning Hamish and setting the entire base of the shaft on fire. [PARAGRAPH]"Go!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Together they slid down the ladder shaft and Amelie hit the burning cellar floor hard. Artan landed on top of her and she immediately pushed him up onto his feet. The grotesque form of Hamish was slapping at itself trying to put the fire out and though he nearly filled the hallway Artan was quickly up and past him. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie slipped in the burning oil and fell when she tried to run. Her coat caught fire and when she got up again Hamish was on her. Hamish grabbed her sleeve and pulled her against the bare skin of his living suit. Amelie could feel the dank sweat of the hanging man, could smell his rotting flesh and looked up to see two pairs of eyes staring back at her. Hamish's sparkled with dark pleasure, and the hanging man looked equally horrified and helpless. [PARAGRAPH]Artan came running back down the hall. He had one of the knives from the room with the stone table in his hand. Before Hamish turned Artan leapt at him, stabbing clear through the hanging man's back and into Hamish. [PARAGRAPH]The jolt of pain was enough for Amelie to unfasten her coat and slip out of Hamish's grip. She ran by him, grabbing Artan as she went. [PARAGRAPH]They ran past the four archways to where stairs lead up into darkness. Hamish thundered down the hallway behind them and his elongated shadow was reflected on every surface by the fire burning under the ladder shaft. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie could barely make out a closed door at the top of the stairs and she prayed as she charged toward it that it would open. She hit it full speed and it flew open. [PARAGRAPH]Both children popped up into a long kitchen. A pot boiled in a fireplace, ovens were set against one wall and tables were covered with trays and bowls. A tray of freshly baked cookies sat out, half covered in green frosting. The room smelled of gingerbread and vanilla. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie and Artan were stunned by the change in scenery. The room seemed cozy and welcoming, homey in a way their home had never been. But the sound of Hamish on the stairs reminded them they were still in danger. [PARAGRAPH]"Close the door!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung the door closed while Amelie searched for the bar used to brace it. She found it on the counter nearest the door and raced to slide it through the four iron braces on the back of the door. It had only gone through the first when Hamish hit the door. [PARAGRAPH]For a brief second the door looked like it may hold, but then, in an explosion of splintering wood, the door flew open and Hamish came stumbling up into the kitchen. Once again, the children were off running. Artan threw open the door on the far end of the kitchen, revealing a short hallway that ended at a room the children recognized, the front room of the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]They ran through the front room, past the shelves of jars and treats they had dreamed about for so long. Artan went to the front door, but Amelie ran to the low bench in front of the window. [PARAGRAPH]The door was locked. [PARAGRAPH]"Help me. " Amelie yelled as she lifted one end of the bench. [PARAGRAPH]Artan grabbed the other end and as Hamish entered the front room the children threw the bench through the huge front window. Amelie and Artan leapt through the shattered window behind it. [PARAGRAPH]The children screamed for help as they ran up the hill toward the temple. Hamish continued his pursuit, and though the glass shards cut up the hanging man's feet, he raced after them. If he had looked crazed in the nightmare of the cellar, he looked even more so in the ordinary city night. A man wearing another man's body as a second skin running through the streets of Bourne. [PARAGRAPH]Despite his cut feet Hamish was faster than the children on the straight road. And if anyone heard the calls for help, they weren't responding. [PARAGRAPH]By the time Amelie reached the temple, her terror had been replaced with exhaustion. She could barely breathe, she felt like she was choking, and her heart was racing so fast it made her dizzy. Amelie collapsed against the temple door and turned the handle, for the first time wondering if the temple would even be unlocked. [PARAGRAPH]It was unlocked, but where Amelie expected the warm glow of safety or an army of priests and angels set to protect them, there was only the cold, lifeless interior of the temple. The pews were empty and the stained-glass windows dark. The clear round window that formed the top of the church was the only real source of light. Through it moonlight shone down on the center of the temple, highlighting the altar. [PARAGRAPH]"Put your hand on the altar and don't let go. " Amelie commanded. [PARAGRAPH]Artan looked less convinced, his eyes widened in fear when he realized this door was the only way into, or out of, the temple. They would be trapped here. [PARAGRAPH]There was no time to try to close the door behind them, Hamish was in the doorway right behind them. As the children ran to the center of the small temple Hamish stopped to look around. It seemed that he may also have expected some sort of defense here, though he was obviously pleased to see that the temple was empty. He closed the temple door behind him. [PARAGRAPH]"For a moment I thought you might get away. " Hamish said smiling. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish stretched in the hanging man's skin, the sight was grotesque and unnerving. Bones creaked and popped and the cord binding the chest together pulled taunt against the loose flesh. Above Hamish's head the hanging man's eyes fluttered back and forth in fear as if looking for something in the room. [PARAGRAPH]"You can't hurt us here. " Amelie said, her hand firmly on the Altar's warm mahogany top. [PARAGRAPH]"Are we playing some of game?" Hamish asked, "Is this your base? I'm afraid I may have to break the rules. "[PARAGRAPH]Hamish walked down the center aisle toward them. [PARAGRAPH]"You dropped this. " Hamish said, holding out Amelie's burnt coat. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't move. Artan fidgeted beside her, he still held the knife with one hand and gripped the altar with the other. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm glad you followed your brother. " Hamish said, "You will make a wonderful offering. And I can keep your brother to fatten up. "[PARAGRAPH]At that Hamish charged the altar. Just before Hamish hit them Artan let go of the altar and stepped in front of his sister, swinging wildly with his knife. [PARAGRAPH]"No!" Amelie screamed, grabbing Artan's free hand. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish caught Artan's knife hand in a fist so large it nearly covered up Artan's entire forearm. Hamish pushed down on the back of Artan's hand with his thumb, forcing him to drop the knife, then with a sickening pop Artan's wrist broke. [PARAGRAPH]Artan screamed in pain. And though Amelie pulled, her brother was caught between them. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish towered over the children, Amelie barely came to his waist and as Hamish pulled the screaming Artan away, Amelie's finger slid easily across the smooth altar. She stretched as her fingers came to the edge of the altar. Just as her fingertips were all that was left of her contact with the altar she let go of Artan's hand. [PARAGRAPH]"Shhh. . . " Hamish whispered to the crying boy. Hamish lifted Artan, placing one meaty hand over Artan's mouth. Three sets of eyes looked down at Amelie, but she stood unmoving, hand once again firmly on the altar. Tears silently pouring down her face. [PARAGRAPH]Without saying anything Hamish turned and walked out of the temple, carrying the struggling Artan with him. When he was gone Amelie collapsed beside the altar, with her hand still on it, and cried so violently that her small body shook with each wail and ragged coughing breath. That is where they found her the next morning, though Hamish and Artan were gone.

The Foxmen are a cult of Tali, God of the Wind. He has no formal priesthood but many shrines built in the most remote and dangerous parts of Erebus. Some say the Foxmen put them there just to give each other excuses to travel. The Foxmen are renowned for their Wanderlust. They cannot stand to stay still for very long. There are no better explorers than their Drifters, nor better story tellers. The closest thing to a mass religious service are the convocations that they Foxmen are known to hold on the rooftops of popular inns, where they regale each other with tall tales of their past or future exploits. Ceridwen, Goddess of the Stars, of Magic,and of the Social Relationships that bind mortals together, is served by numerous cults with only tenuous ties to one another. [PARAGRAPH:2]Ceridwen first appeared to a suicidal Kylorin, asking him to worship her in exchange for arcane knowledge and the power to resurrect his wife indefinitely so they might restart their marriage untainted by her adultery. He attempted to make her cult into the State Religion of Patria, but only a small group of elites ever accepted her tenets. The most elite of the elites were the Coven of the Black Candle, whom she tasked with blotting out The Sun. This Coven consisted of Kylorin himself, Os-Gabella, Asmoday, Faeryl Viconia, Alexis, Barbatos, and "Wode"-who was actually the God of Shadow masquerading as the mortal master of Shadow magic. Esus transformed his Seven Aspects (the greatest of his True Angels besides Iaegus) into the Masks each Coven member wore, so that no power in creation could detect or control them. The members could never learn each other's identity, as the animus between Asmoday and the Fey would have made their cooperation impossible. [PARAGRAPH:1]A lesser Masked Coven, called "The Between," continues to this day. It is a small religion whose members are mostly sorceresses whose spirits, minds and occasionally bodies explore worlds beyond Erebus. Many are driven mad by the experience. They refer to their goddesses as the Maiden of the Mask. [PARAGRAPH:1]Among the Sheaim there is a cult filled with a missionary zeal to reach all nations and bring their best and brightest back to learn sorcery without the strictures and limitations placed on adepts by mage guilds in all other lands. They promise unfettered access to secret knowledge of all sorts, but tend to steer their students into the darkest of arts. The Emrys have a goal more grand that blotting our the son. They want to bring on Armageddon and end Erebus entirely. [PARAGRAPH:1]Not all of her worshipers are that evil. The Chainbreakers have more noble goals. They believe the goddess is best served by breaking unjust social bonds. They hate any relationship that is not entirely consensual. Some try to destroy marriages and turn children against their parents, but most focus their radical activism on fighting for the abolition of slavery. They can always be counted upon to provide aid and sanctuary to runaway slaves, but prefer to give them arms and help them slay their former masters. The Ring-givers' faith is practiced through artifice. Each accomplishment or blessing is added to their collection of charms, rings and baubles. Judges sought out to adjudicate between different parties. Their religion preaches against bias and imparts decisions without local or personal influence. Mechanic: The Grey Council is a voting body where the player can participate in elections with other players. Often called the Adjudicator.

The church of Bhall has little long-lasting structure. Instead religious upheavals happen and huge masses of fanatical followers rise up and rebel against whatever is being protested in that area. The cause is less important than the fervor, the blessing of Bhall, and the violence that comes with the rebellion. Most worshipers of Bhall receive a brand of her mark that forever burns and inflicts pain. Bhall is also known as the Queen of Fire and the Fallen Star.

The church of Camulos wants war between all nations. He is known as the Sanguine Fountain and the Hundred Armed God. On the nights before large battles, the skies echo with the shrill cries of Camulos's demons, peering out expectantly for the coming war. In cities that don't outlaw them, temples to Camulos are brutal arenas where corpses of the freshly killed lie in piles, feral animals feast on the bodies, and nearly every stone is blood stained. This is a religion based on hate. It is racist in some countries, anti-cultural group in others. The target doesn't matter to the religion, only the hate that is fueled by it.

[TAB]Junil, the elder of the Gods, had promised to stay apart from the conflict in Creation. While other gods pressed the limits of the Compact or blatantly ignored it, he held to its restrictions and spirit. Even when his church was a mockery of his dominion, he would not respond. It was only when the compact was openly broken, when fallen angels walked in creation that he responded to help the least of men. He asked only one thing in return: unquestioning obedience. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Order was founded during the Age of Magic, not from divine inspiration but from the growing requirements of the Patrian bureaucracy. The codex of Patrian law had become so byzantine and severe that nearly autonomous inquisitors were needed to carry out it requirements. These inquisitors were magically bound to the codex so that they wouldn't become corrupted by their station. They drew upon the name of Junil, God of Law, in taking their oaths and in carrying out their brutal decrees. [PARAGRAPH:1]These inquisitors were feared nearly as much as Kylorin's Archmages and would come to a city to adjudicate major disputes and to see that justice, as defined by the codex of Patria, was followed. [PARAGRAPH:1]At the head of the church was Soqed Hozi. It is said that if she spoke a lie, reality would change to make it into truth. Soqed had a mute twin who was little more than a dim shadow of her powerful sister. The two remained at the Temple of Atonement where they oversaw the church and its inquisitors. [PARAGRAPH:1]The ideology of Junil was secondary to the church's task of maintaining the laws of Patria. Some lesser confessors began to question: "What was the use of following the law if it was corrupt?". The most conflicted of these was Sphener, an inquisitor who killed demons in his service to the church. He had gazed into hell and it was only his strict adherence to his faith that allowed him to survive. Sphener obeyed every edict of the church, but argued that worship of Junil was the greatest mission of the church. [PARAGRAPH:1]The church found out about the whispered concerns of some of its members and launched the Purge of Whispers, and attempt to execute anyone in the church who questioned church doctrine. [PARAGRAPH:1]The purge was horribly effective and killed members of the church, family and friends. It covered many cities over all of Patria and happened in a single night. Sphener was one of the few that escaped the purge and the next day the church held a trial for him in absentia. They convicted him and sentenced him to death upon the wheel. Condemned by his law, his church, and his god, Sphener came to the church on his own and accepted his execution. He was broken as the church elders and the public watched. [PARAGRAPH:1]Over the next decade Sphener's spirit was seen hundreds of times tending to those in need. He tended to those unfairly persecuted by the church and ministered to church members that prayed to Junil for guidance. This became the basis for the new Order church that would be founded in the Age of Rebirth. [TAB]Where the Order values law, the Empyrean values wisdom. Adjudication started from the teachings of Lugus and punishment is not based on adherence to a labyrinthine codex of laws, but from direct consultation on the merits of each case. Social equality and impartiality are the model between a government and its citizens as well as between empires. As such the Empyrean gives equal voice to small empires as it does those that dominate Erebus. [TAB]Kilmorph is the goddess of the earth, She Who Dwells Beneath. She formed children out of stone, the Dwarves, and taught them the secrets of metalworking. One of the first religions available to the men of the world, Kilmorph will answer the prayers of honorable men and even send her soldiers to defend their cities. [TAB]Deep in the woods, the whispers of Elves linger. Ancient protectors normally above the affairs of men, some men have shown enough loyalty to them to be taught their magic and even gain the assistance of the Satyrs. [TAB]The power beneath the Aegean waves is said to be more powerful than any other, but the Undertow are unfocused and follow a thousand different obscure agendas. The Disciples of the Undertow dare not expose themselves directly to the conflicting commands of their masters and instead use the poor as intermediaries. They are quickly driven insane by the process, which the disciples prefer as it keeps them from manipulating the message. They also share the process of turning a warrior into The Drown, undead thralls, a process with few volunteers. [TAB]A secret council that is so good at spreading lies that it is often unaware of the truth of its own stories. They have "thrones" (secret meeting places) in most major cities and excel at sneaking goods and people into or out of areas. Esus is known as the King of Thieves, Jack Shadow, and Moonsong, though it's popular for religious leaders to take these names for themselves as well. [PARAGRAPH:2]Founding[PARAGRAPH]This is the most common legend spread about the founding of the religion. No one knows if it's actually true. [PARAGRAPH]Unknown to the other gods, Esus slips into creation from time to time. Most commonly as a traveling minstrel (male or female as it suits him), but occasionally as a merchant, beggar, jackal or crow. [PARAGRAPH]On one of these trips he met Oriol Peregrinus, a priest of Kilmorph who had been stealing from his temple for years. The night before he was to go face trial he sat in a bar drinking and whispering prayers to any god that would hear him, as his own certainly wouldn't forgive his crime. [PARAGRAPH]Esus, who was playing at the bar, overheard him and went to comfort the man. The two shared drinks and eventually Oriol shared his story. Esus offered a lie that Oriol could tell to the church, but Oriol was still worried that he wouldn't be believed. At that Esus offered him an opal scarab that would make anyone believe his lies. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol took the scarab and went to his trial before the church elders. To his surprise, they believed his lies without question. Those that accused him were punished and it increased his standing in the church of Kilmorph. [PARAGRAPH]A year later Esus returned and found Oriol at the bar again. This time he was ruined, he barely had the money to pay for his drink and had lost everything in the world that mattered to him. Esus asked what was wrong and he said that no one believed anything he said. He thought the scarab was cursed and threw it away. [PARAGRAPH]Esus explained that he had made the man's lies believable, but at a cost that no one would believe anything Oriol said that was true. If Oriol told his wife he loved her, she wouldn't believe him. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol sobbed into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"What is your name?" Esus asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Oriol. " Oriol said, still staring into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't believe you. " Esus said. "I think your name is Mendax Opacous. "[PARAGRAPH]"My name is Mendax?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"That sounds better. That is a name people will believe. " Esus said. "And what god do you worship? Surely not Kilmorph, I think you worship Esus, the god of shadows. "[PARAGRAPH]"I worship the god of shadows?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Yes you do. See how easy this is. " Esus said. "And remember that you can tell any woman you love her, and she will believe you. As long as it isn't true. If you actually love her then your words will be sour to her ears, your affections will poison her against you. You can go to a new city, start a new life, raise up a church to Esus, as long as you know that it is all pretend. "[PARAGRAPH]"I have already lost my wife's love to your curse. " Oriol said. "I have lost my standing in the church, you should have me abandon my faith as well? What if I just go to church elders and tell them about what you have done to me?"[PARAGRAPH]"You could try, but who would believe you?" Esus said with a smile. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol, now going by Mendax, did as Esus suggested and founded the first Aphotic Throne in an abandoned Patrian manor (it was easy enough to convince them that he was the real owner). The traditions of that throne were largely made up by him in a tangled weave of whatever inspiration struck him in the moment. It was said that his biggest secret was that he kept a small shrine of Kilmorph until the day he died. [PARAGRAPH:3]Sects[PARAGRAPH]Every Throne could be considered its own sect. There is no common communication, rules or traditions between them. Some are brutal and vengeful, others are lighthearted and free. They tend to be the opposite of the communities they exist in. Sometimes they are the secret power behind the city government, and sometimes they are teenage adventurers pretending at being a secret organization. [PARAGRAPH:3]An oddity among the religions, the Council of Esus has no temples or ordinary disciples. As a secret society, it cannot be [LINK=SPELL_EVANGELIZE]Evangelized[\LINK] openly to either cities or all the units nearby. However, any unit which is a member can pay to establish a local Council presence in any city. Units without another State Religion prerequisite, and with a leader with the right State Religion, can spend gold to purchase an initiation from an Esus [LINK=PROMOTION_EVANGELIZE]Evangelist[\LINK] on the same plot. That theme, paying for miracles, is common in the Council of Esus. [PARAGRAPH]Esus's priests have the abilities of Spies, including the ability to steal plans, destroy city production, and sabotage improvements including even Unique Features. [PARAGRAPH]State Religion allows access to the [LINK=UNIT_SHADOWRIDER]Shadowrider[\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_ESUS]Swindler [\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_ESUS]Thief[\LINK], and [LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_ESUS]Propogandist[\LINK] units. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus has major conflicts with The Empyrean. One may prevent the spread of another into a city, or drive the other out. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus was the driving force behind the founding of the Undercouncil in opposition to the Overcouncil. No player may adopt the Undercouncil civic until this religion is founded, nor may any player with this state religion join the Overcouncil.

It will be weakened in Good lands, strengthened in Neutral or Evil lands.It will be strengthened by proximity to [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]Shadow Mana[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WODES_OAK]Wode's Oak[\LINK], and the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WHISPERING_WOOD]Whispering Wood[\LINK], It is weakened by [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SUN]Sun Mana[\LINK], the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MIRROR_OF_HEAVEN]Mirror of Heaven[\LINK], and [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL_OF_LIGHT]Citadels of Light[\LINK].

[TAB]Mages spent weeks in meditation, exploring the farthest reaches of the ethereal world. The demands of the body were ignored, and they survived sustained only by magic. Their efforts were rewarded, a sentience was contacted, dark and horrible. It whispered secrets into the mages' minds, secrets of necromancy, diseases, and sacrificial rites. It promised power in exchange for their blood, and they freely gave it.
